domain_label: Sweater Vertical — Knitting-Machine Acquisition Economics & Buy-vs-Subcontract
purpose: A session-bounded method for a micro D2C acrylic/acrylic-blend knitwear brand sourcing knit+link+finish in Ludhiana to decide HOW to acquire knitting, linking and finishing capacity across a phased path — Phase 0 subcontract into the Ludhiana job-work mesh, Phase 1 buy used (Chinese Cixing-class first), new only Shima or Chinese with Stoll new-build off the table after the 2025 Karl Mayer exit — by consolidating wide [ESTIMATE] cost bands per machine class, throughput bands that prove linking caps daily output, the HSN 8447 import stack, and a recomputing buy-vs-subcontract breakeven on utilisation, without ever stating a fabricated named-builder price as fact.
assumptions: no landed vendor quote is supplied; every price, MOQ, throughput, lead-time and breakeven figure is a labeled [ESTIMATE] with stated method, basis and confidence, never a fake-precise figure presented as [FACT] for any named machine builder (Shima, Stoll, Cixing, Steiger)

the user is a deliberately tiny, fast-iterating acrylic/acrylic-blend capsule brand selling D2C in California/Turlock and sourcing knit-link-finish capacity through the Ludhiana job-work mesh, not a volume manufacturer

the Stoll/KARL MAYER 2025 flat-knit exit, HSN heading 8447, the 18% IGST rate and Groz-Beckert needle supply are cited public [FACT]; the exact BCD sub-heading rate and any 2025-26 budget change carry their own [ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tag and must be confirmed at purchase
Ludhiana dealer existence (Kniton Traders, King International) and India-as-importer are public-existence facts, not a confirmed supply contract for this brand unless a source states the relationship

throughput, capacity, utilisation and cost bands are order-of-magnitude planning priors drawn from industry-lore and vendor literature, not audited per-machine logs; coverage is a floor and [UNKNOWN] is a frequent, valid value
exclusions: stating a fabricated dollar figure for a specifically named machine builder as fact rather than as a labeled [ESTIMATE] band
the machine-family taxonomy and what each family does mechanically (owned by the sibling machine-landscape KB) except where an acquisition decision straddles into it
the yarn-side, finishing-chemistry, QC, brand and unit-economics deep-dives owned by the other specialists (T2, T6, T5, T7, T9) except where a machine-acquisition decision straddles into them

a committed financial pro forma or cost model for an owned line (rebuilt bottom-up against a real Ludhiana unit in T4); this models the acquisition decision and its breakeven structure, not the financial plan
tax, import-licensing and IP-legal advice for a specific transaction; this models the acquisition path and the duty stack at band level, not a specific filing

competency_questions.question: What is the phased acquisition decision in priority order, and why does Phase 0 default to subcontract rather than ownership?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACQUISITION_PHASES states Phase 0 subcontract knit+link+finish into the Ludhiana mesh (plus optional one cheap used hand-flat for sampling), Phase 1 buy 1-2 used machines at proven volume, and new only as a later benchmark, and SUBCONTRACT_PHASE0 explains the agglomeration-is-infrastructure and capital-stays-free-for-CAC rationale

competency_questions.question: When does buying a used machine become correct, and which tier is the default first buy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUY_USED_THRESHOLD states used buying is justified only when one repeating program at sustained volume fills the machine, programmer and linkers, and names the Chinese Cixing-class tier as the default first used buy

competency_questions.question: When is buying a NEW machine ever the move, and which builders remain on the table after the Stoll exit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUY_NEW_THRESHOLD states new is rarely a founding move and only a volume/quality-benchmark purchase, and that new-build narrows to Shima (premium, India support) or Chinese (Cixing, cost tier) because Stoll new-build is off the table

competency_questions.question: What are the consolidated price bands per machine class, and how are they kept honest when no landed quote is in hand?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICE_BANDS_ESTIMATE gives wide new and used bands per class (hand-flat, power-flat, Chinese computerised, Shima/Stoll standard FF, whole-garment, linking, automatic Italian linker, finishing) each labeled [ESTIMATE] with confidence, and explicitly downgrades tidy single anchors like a ~$15k used Chinese machine to wide LOW-MED bands needing a landed quote

competency_questions.question: Why do throughput bands show that linking, not knitting, caps daily output, and how does that bound a buy decision?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: THROUGHPUT_LINK_CAP gives the per-shift knit-vs-link-vs-whole-garment bands as labeled estimates and shows the arithmetic that makes linking the binding ceiling, so any machine buy must be matched by linker and programmer capacity

competency_questions.question: What import cost does a knitting machine carry into India under HSN 8447, and what hidden landed costs ride alongside?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: IMPORT_DUTY_HSN8447 names HS heading 8447, the ~7.5% BCD (+ surcharge) + 18% IGST working stack as a labeled estimate-on-the-sub-heading with 18% IGST cited [FACT], and lists install, power/compressed-air, spares and ex-Stoll Obertshausen service as hidden landed costs

competency_questions.question: How is the buy-vs-subcontract breakeven computed on utilisation, and what utilisation flips the decision?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BREAKEVEN_UTILISATION states the formula breakeven_utilisation = owned_fixed_period_cost / ((jobwork_unit_rate - owned_variable_unit_cost) * period_capacity) and recomputes it as a labeled estimate, concluding that below the breakeven utilisation subcontract wins and only a repeating program at sustained volume clears it

competency_questions.question: Why is building your own knitting machine the highest-confidence do-not, and where does that leave acquisition?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUILD_NEVER states the core kinematic chain (bed, needles, cams, electronic selection, firmware, knit-CAD) is decades-deep and supplier-defended (Groz-Beckert makes the needles even for Shima and Stoll), gives the ~$2M-10M+/3-7yr direction-only estimate versus a sub-$20k used machine, and confines acquisition to subcontract-or-buy

competency_questions.question: How does the 2025 Stoll/KARL MAYER flat-knit exit reshape the used pool and the buy decision?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STOLL_EXIT_USED_SHIFT states the cited 2025 discontinuation and Reutlingen closure, that new-build narrows to Shima plus Chinese, that the installed base deepens the used pool reinforcing buy-used, and that ex-Stoll parts-via-Obertshausen is now a diligence item on any ex-Stoll used buy

competency_questions.question: Where does India sit in the acquisition market, and what does the importer/dealer structure mean for sourcing a machine?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INDIA_IMPORTER_MARKET states India is an importer/assembler/dealer market not a builder of computerised flats, names Ludhiana dealers handling Shima/Stoll/Cixing plus parts and repair, and frames every buy as an import-and-dealer transaction not a local-OEM purchase

competency_questions.question: How is whole-garment acquisition weighed, given it deletes linking but is the highest capital and steepest programming?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WHOLEGARMENT_ACQUISITION states whole-garment deletes the linker bottleneck but is the most expensive class with the steepest programming, prices it as a wide [ESTIMATE] band, and frames it as a later volume trade study, never a launch buy

competency_questions.question: What diligence must any used-machine buy pass before the cost model commits?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: USED_MACHINE_DILIGENCE lists the mechanical condition (bed flatness, needle/cam wear, gauge), the program/toolchain-lock check, the spares-and-service availability (ex-Stoll Obertshausen-only), and the get-a-landed-quote gate as the #1 input gap into T4

competency_questions.question: How is acquisition cost modeled honestly without asserting any named builder's actual price, and how is a band labeled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONESTY_BAND_DISCIPLINE derives every money/throughput figure as a labeled [ESTIMATE] band with method, basis and confidence (or [FACT]/[UNKNOWN]), tags the Stoll exit / HSN 8447 / 18% IGST / Groz-Beckert items [FACT], and states the landed-quote confirmation path

competency_questions.question: Given phases, bands, the duty stack, the breakeven and market structure, what is the merged acquisition verdict and how is it kept current?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACQUISITION_VERDICT composes subcontract-at-capsule, buy-used-Chinese-first-at-proven-volume, new-rarely and build-never into a defensible call gated on the breakeven, and ACQUISITION_REVIEW_LOOP sets the landed-quote / volume / Stoll-exit-effect / duty-change triggers that re-run the decision

glossary.definition: The binding honesty label on every money, capacity, throughput, lead-time and breakeven figure in this KB: a reasoned band with stated method, basis and confidence carrying the literal word estimate, never a fake-precise figure presented as [FACT] for any named machine builder; tidy single anchors like a ~$15k used Chinese machine are decision-framing illustrations downgraded to wide LOW-MED bands needing a landed quote.

The launch/capsule acquisition posture: subcontract knit + link + finish into the Ludhiana job-work mesh and own only design, brand and optionally one cheap used hand-flat (~$200-1,500 [ESTIMATE, MED]) for in-house sampling, keeping capital free for design and CAC instead of buying iron.

The proven-volume acquisition posture: buy 1-2 USED machines (Chinese Cixing-class first) plus a CAD seat, spares and matching linkers, justified only once one repeating program at sustained volume fills the machine, the programmer and the linkers.

The utilisation fraction at which an owned line's per-period fixed cost is just covered by the per-unit conversion saving over job-work: breakeven_utilisation = owned_fixed_period_cost / ((jobwork_unit_rate - owned_variable_unit_cost) * period_capacity); below it subcontract wins, above it owning a used machine wins, computed as a labeled [ESTIMATE].

The duty stack a knitting machine carries into India: HS heading 8447 bearing ~7.5% BCD (+ ~0.75% surcharge) then 18% IGST on assessable value [FACT on heading and 18% IGST; ESTIMATE on the exact BCD sub-heading, confirm at purchase], plus hidden install, power/compressed-air, spares and ex-Stoll Obertshausen service costs.

KARL MAYER (which acquired Stoll in 2020) decided in early 2025 to discontinue the STOLL flat-knitting machine business; the Reutlingen plant closed 31 Oct 2025, China production ended Dec 2025, spares/service continue only via the Obertshausen warehouse [FACT] — narrowing new-build to Shima plus Chinese and deepening the used pool, which reinforces buy-used.

A used Chinese computerised flat machine (Cixing leads the tier; Cixing also owns Switzerland's Steiger) at the cost end of the market, the default first used buy at ~$4,000-15,000 [ESTIMATE, MED] because the used pool is deep and post-Stoll deepening.

Buying a seamless whole-garment machine (Shima WHOLEGARMENT / Stoll knit&wear) that deletes the linker bottleneck but is the most expensive class (~$120,000-250,000+ new, ~$20,000-90,000 used [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED]) with the steepest programming; a later volume trade study, never a launch buy.

The structural fact that India imports and deals computerised flat machines rather than building them: Ludhiana dealers (Kniton Traders, King International) handle Shima/Stoll/Cixing plus parts and repair [FACT existence], so every machine buy is an import-and-dealer transaction with HSN 8447 duty, not a local-OEM purchase.

The pre-commit checklist on any used buy: mechanical condition (bed flatness, needle/cam wear, gauge), the vendor-locked program/toolchain (a Shima program is not a Stoll program), spares-and-service availability (ex-Stoll Obertshausen-only), and a real landed quote (machine + freight + duty + install) — the #1 input gap into the T4 cost model.

nodes.definition: Establish the phased acquisition decision in priority order for a micro fully-fashioned sweater line, because the make-vs-buy boundary moves with proven volume. Phase 0 (launch/capsule): subcontract knit + link + finish into the Ludhiana job-work mesh, optionally buy one cheap used hand-flat (~$200-1,500 [ESTIMATE, MED]) for in-house sampling only, and spend instead on a knit-CAD seat, a contracted programmer and sampling. Phase 1 (one style proven at volume): buy 1-2 USED machines, Chinese Cixing-class first, plus a CAD seat, spares and linkers to match output. New machine: only a later volume/quality-benchmark purchase, Shima or Chinese, never a founding move. This phased order is the spine every downstream cost, duty and breakeven judgment hangs on.

included: the Phase 0 subcontract / Phase 1 buy-used / new-later ordering
the optional cheap sampling hand-flat at Phase 0
the proven-volume trigger that moves the boundary

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the proven-volume trigger or the phase order changes

pros.claim: Sequencing the decision by proven volume keeps capital out of iron until utilisation justifies it
pros.example: a capsule brand subcontracting at launch and only buying a used Cixing-class machine once one style repeats at volume

cons.claim: A fixed phase order can lag a genuine early opportunity, e.g. a bargain used machine appearing before Phase 1 volume
cons.example: passing a well-priced used machine because the phase gate has not formally opened

failure_modes: buying iron at Phase 0 capsule scale before any style repeats at volume
treating the sampling hand-flat as production capacity rather than an iteration tool
acceptance_tests: the node states the Phase 0 subcontract, Phase 1 buy-used-Chinese-first and new-later ordering and the proven-volume trigger that advances the phase
revisit_triggers: a style reaches proven repeating volume
a bargain used machine appears before the phase gate
the subcontract mesh's capacity or rates change

nodes.definition: Establish why subcontracting knit + link + finish into the Ludhiana job-work mesh is the right Phase 0 acquisition posture for a capsule brand. The agglomeration is the infrastructure — the one Ludhiana moat that helps a tiny brand, because spinners, knitters, linkers, finishers and machine dealers sit within reach and share specialised steps at small batch. Subcontracting keeps capital free for design and CAC, fits the small, fast, varied runs an AI-design brand lives on, and avoids the mid-six-figure-plus skilled-staffing commitment (illustratively ~2-4 knitters + 2-4 linkers + finishing + >=1 programmer for ~30-60 sweaters/day [ESTIMATE: design illustration, LOW-MED]) that an owned line demands before a single garment sells. Own only design, brand and optionally one cheap used hand-flat for sampling.

included: the agglomeration-is-infrastructure rationale
capital-stays-free-for-design-and-CAC
the mid-six-figure owned-line illustration as a labeled estimate

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: job-work rates, mesh capacity, or the buy-used trigger changes

pros.claim: Subcontracting rents the scarce skills and shares capacity at small batch so capital stays on design and CAC
pros.example: a brand routing knit, link and finish across tiny Ludhiana vendors and spending the saved capital on customer acquisition

cons.claim: A job-work mesh fragments quality control across many vendors and surrenders direct process control
cons.example: a capsule run whose seam quality varies because linking was spread across several job-workers

failure_modes: committing to an owned line at capsule scale and carrying skilled payroll before a garment sells
under-gating quality across a fragmented subcontract chain
acceptance_tests: the node states the agglomeration-is-infrastructure and capital-stays-free rationale and gives the owned-line commitment as a labeled estimate against the subcontract alternative
revisit_triggers: job-work knit/link rates per piece become available
the mesh's small-batch capacity tightens
a style's volume approaches the buy-used threshold

Used Chinese computerised flat bands ~$4,000-15,000 [ESTIMATE, MED]; add a CAD seat, spares and linkers to match output. Used, not new, is the default proven-volume move.

nodes.definition: Lay down the consolidated new-and-used price bands per machine class, every figure a labeled [ESTIMATE] (two analysts published partly-overlapping bands; where they diverged the wider range and lower confidence are kept rather than splitting into false precision). Hand-flat/domestic sampling: new ~$500-3,000 / used ~$200-1,500 [MED]. Power-flat semi-auto: ~$3,000-10,000 / ~$1,000-5,000 [MED]. Chinese computerised flat (Cixing-class): ~$8,000-40,000+ / ~$4,000-15,000 [MED]. Shima/Stoll computerised flat standard FF: ~$60,000-140,000 / ~$8,000-60,000+ [LOW-MED]. Whole-garment: ~$120,000-250,000+ / ~$20,000-90,000 [LOW-MED]. Linking rotary hand/electric: ~$1,500-8,000 / ~$500-4,000 [MED]. Automatic Italian linker (Complett/Exacta-class): ~$15,000-40,000+ / ~$5,000-20,000 [LOW]. Finishing per unit: ~$2,000-20,000 / ~$1,000-8,000 [LOW-MED]. Get real landed quotes before any cost model commits.

nodes.definition: Lay down the order-of-magnitude throughput bands that prove linking, not knitting, caps daily output, all [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED]: a computerised flat knits one sweater's panels in ~20-45 min (~12-25 garments'-worth of panels/machine/shift); a linker does one sweater's joins in ~10-25 min (~20-45 sweaters/linker/shift); whole-garment is slower per garment (~6-15/machine/shift) but deletes linking entirely. Because the linker band is the binding ceiling, any machine buy must be sized against linker and programmer capacity, not knitting-machine count — buying a faster knitting machine without matching linker capacity just moves idle iron. These are planning bands, not vendor logs; their job is to bound an acquisition against the binding step.

nodes.definition: Establish that the binding capacity an acquisition must match is the linker and the CAD/flat-knit programmer, not the knitting machine. The linker is the eyesight-intensive, hand-skilled, piece-rate seaming step that sets a small line's daily ceiling, and the programmer is the scarce, machine-specific, vendor-locked skill (Shima SDS-ONE APEX/APEXFiz vs Stoll M1plus/knitelligence — a Shima program is not a Stoll program) that turns a design into a runnable machine program. T1 flagged linkers as the hardest role to re-hire and CAD/flat-knit programmers as scarce relative to operators [FACT — T1 Ludhiana DEEPDIVE S4/S6]. Acquiring a machine without securing matching linker and programmer capacity buys dead iron — so every buy decision is really a buy-machine-plus-linkers-plus-programmer decision.

included: the linker as the throughput-setting hand skill
the CAD/flat-knit programmer as the scarce machine-specific skill
the buy-machine-plus-linkers-plus-programmer framing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: linker or programmer availability, wage, or AI-assist on programming changes

pros.claim: Naming linker and programmer as the binding capacity stops a machine being bought without the people to fill it
pros.example: a used-machine buy paired with a contracted programmer and matched linkers rather than iron alone

cons.claim: Linker and programmer availability are human-skill variables that resist clean capacity planning from a spec sheet
cons.example: a buy whose real output swings with which linkers and programmer are actually present

failure_modes: buying a machine with no secured programmer and leaving it as dead iron
sizing a buy off knitting capacity and starving the linkers
acceptance_tests: the node states the linker and the programmer as the binding capacity, the vendor-locked toolchain non-portability, and the buy-machine-plus-linkers-plus-programmer framing
revisit_triggers: a linker labour shortage or wage change
local programmer availability or cost shifts
AI design-to-program assist materially relaxes the programmer constraint

nodes.definition: Account for the import-duty stack a knitting machine carries into India, because it sits on top of every price band and moves the landed cost. Knitting machines fall under HS heading 8447, carrying ~7.5% BCD (+ ~0.75% surcharge) then 18% IGST on assessable value [FACT — HS heading 8447 and 18% IGST; ESTIMATE on the exact BCD sub-heading rate, confirm at purchase]. The exact India BCD sub-heading rate and any 2025-26 budget change are a working assumption to verify at the time of purchase, not a fixed fact. This duty stack is why a band price is not a landed price, and it must be added before the breakeven or any cost model uses a machine cost.

18% IGST cited fact vs ESTIMATE on the BCD sub-heading
the band-price-is-not-landed-price point

cons.claim: The exact BCD sub-heading and budget changes are uncertain, so the duty figure is a working estimate not a fixed line

treating the ~7.5% BCD as fixed when the sub-heading rate is an estimate
acceptance_tests: the node names HS heading 8447, the ~7.5% BCD + 18% IGST stack, marks 18% IGST fact and the BCD sub-heading an estimate-to-confirm, and states a band price is not a landed price

nodes.definition: Account for the hidden landed costs that ride alongside the machine price and duty, so a buy is not under-budgeted. Beyond the band price and the HSN 8447 duty stack, an acquisition carries: ocean/inland freight, installation, power and compressed-air infrastructure (a real fixed cost a job-work mesh externalises), spares, and — for any ex-Stoll used buy — the parts-and-service question now answered only via the Obertshausen central warehouse. The honest machine cost into the breakeven is machine band + freight + duty + install + infrastructure + first spares, not the sticker. This stack is exactly why subcontracting externalises capital that ownership must carry, and it is the #1 input gap a landed quote must close before T4 commits a cost model.

included: freight, install, power/compressed-air, spares and ex-Stoll service as landed costs
the full machine-cost-into-breakeven definition
the capital-externalised-by-subcontract point

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a site survey, ex-Stoll service cost, or landed quote changes the stack

pros.claim: Listing the hidden landed costs makes the true owned-machine cost visible against the subcontract alternative
pros.example: a used-machine budget that adds install, power/air and first spares rather than stopping at the band price

nodes.definition: Compute the buy-vs-subcontract breakeven on utilisation as a recomputing labeled [ESTIMATE]. Formula: breakeven_utilisation = owned_fixed_period_cost / ((jobwork_unit_rate - owned_variable_unit_cost) * period_capacity). Owned_fixed_period_cost is the per-period amortised landed machine cost plus programmer and skilled payroll and power/infrastructure; jobwork_unit_rate is the per-sweater conversion charge the mesh quotes; owned_variable_unit_cost is in-house per-sweater yarn-handling, energy and consumables; period_capacity is the linker-bound sweaters the owned line can ship per period. Worked illustration [ESTIMATE: arithmetic, LOW-MED, placeholder inputs]: owned_fixed_period_cost ~$8,000/mo, conversion saving (jobwork_unit_rate - owned_variable_unit_cost) ~$6/sweater, period_capacity ~900 sweaters/mo (linker-bound) -> breakeven_utilisation = 8000 / (6 * 900) = 8000/5400 ~= 1.48, i.e. ABOVE 100% — the line cannot break even at this saving and capacity, so subcontract wins until either the conversion saving rises or fixed cost falls. Below the breakeven utilisation subcontract wins; only a repeating program at sustained volume that fills the linker-bound capacity clears it. Recompute with real job-work rates and a landed quote before T4 commits.

nodes.definition: Establish what actually moves the buy-vs-subcontract breakeven so the decision can be steered, not just computed once. The breakeven falls (ownership gets easier to justify) when: the job-work conversion rate rises relative to in-house variable cost (a bigger per-sweater saving), the landed machine cost falls (a cheaper used Cixing-class buy or lighter duty), or a single repeating program fills the linker-bound period_capacity at high utilisation. It rises (subcontract stays better) when runs are small, fast and varied (the AI-design capsule reality), when the programmer or linkers are scarce and expensive, or when power/infrastructure fixed cost is high. The strategic read: a deliberately tiny, varied capsule brand sits structurally below the breakeven, which is why subcontract is the default and buy-used only follows proven, repeating, single-program volume.

nodes.definition: Account for the single market-structure fact that reshapes the acquisition decision: KARL MAYER (which acquired Stoll in 2020) decided in early 2025 to refocus on warp knitting/technical textiles and discontinue the STOLL flat-knitting machine business. nodes.definition: Weigh whole-garment (Shima WHOLEGARMENT / Stoll knit&wear) as an acquisition: it knits the entire garment in one piece with no linking, so it deletes the linker bottleneck outright — the one capacity ceiling every other buy is sized against. But it is the most expensive class (~$120,000-250,000+ new, ~$20,000-90,000 used [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED]) with the steepest programming (a full 3D integral build demanding the most skilled programmer) and is slower per garment (~6-15/machine/shift [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED]). Its entire strategic value lives in deleting linking, but the micro-economics at capsule scale are net [UNKNOWN]. For a capsule brand it is a later volume trade study, never a launch buy — revisited only once a single style's volume and the cost of linking justify trading the linker bottleneck for the highest capital and programming.

nodes.definition: Establish that building your own knitting machine is the highest-confidence do-not, which confines acquisition to subcontract-or-buy. The core kinematic chain — needle bed, needles, cam systems, electronic needle-selection, controller firmware and knit-CAD software — is decades-deep and supplier-defended: even Shima and Stoll buy their needles from Groz-Beckert [FACT — groz-beckert.com], and every serious open/academic effort (OpenKnit, CMU Textiles Lab, the knitout format, knit compilers) lives on the software layer, not the metal [FACT]. The precision wall (gauge pitch and bed flatness held to a fraction of a millimetre over a 1-1.7 m bed, repeatable after thermal cycling and millions of strokes) is real. Build cost ~$2M-10M+ over 3-7 years for a likely-inferior result [ESTIMATE, HIGH on direction] versus a sub-$20k used Chinese machine that already works. The decision is not close: acquisition means subcontract or buy, never build.

nodes.definition: Establish the diligence any used-machine buy must pass before the cost model commits. Four checks: (1) mechanical condition — bed flatness, needle and cam wear, gauge, and repeatability after the machine's service life, because a band price hides condition; (2) the program/toolchain lock — confirm the vendor-locked CAD toolchain matches the programmer's skill (a Shima program is not a Stoll program), or the machine is dead iron; (3) spares-and-service availability — especially ex-Stoll, now Obertshausen-only, which must be priced into the buy; (4) a real landed quote (machine + freight + duty + install + spares), the #1 input gap into the T4 cost model. Skipping diligence converts an apparent saving into a stranded asset; passing it is the gate between a band and a committed buy.

edge_cases.description: An ex-Stoll used machine is bought without pricing the Obertshausen-only parts-and-service risk
edge_cases.trigger: an ex-Stoll buy ignores the post-2025 service constraint
edge_cases.mitigation: price ex-Stoll spares and service via Obertshausen into the landed cost before buying ex-Stoll iron

edge_cases.description: A new Stoll purchase is planned that is no longer available after the 2025 exit
edge_cases.trigger: a new-build plan assumes Stoll flat-knit is still sold
edge_cases.mitigation: narrow any new-build to Shima or Chinese; treat new Stoll flat-knit as end-of-line

edge_cases.description: A machine-build program is entertained to own the technology
edge_cases.trigger: a build-cheap myth resurfaces in planning
edge_cases.mitigation: rule out build (~$2M-10M+/3-7yr for a likely-inferior result) and buy a sub-$20k working used machine instead

edge_cases.description: A whole-garment machine is bought at launch scale before volume justifies its capital and programming
edge_cases.trigger: the no-linking upside is chased before proven volume
edge_cases.mitigation: buy panelled used plus linkers first; open the whole-garment trade study only at sustained single-style volume

edge_cases.description: A band price is used as a landed price and the import is under-budgeted
edge_cases.trigger: the HSN 8447 duty and hidden landed costs are omitted from the machine cost
edge_cases.mitigation: add ~7.5% BCD + 18% IGST plus freight, install, power/air and spares before the cost enters the breakeven

edge_cases.description: A named-builder price is stated as fact instead of a labeled estimate band
edge_cases.trigger: a price figure is quoted without an [ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tag and confidence
edge_cases.mitigation: express every cost as a labeled estimate band with method/basis/confidence and a landed-quote confirmation path

edge_cases.description: A cheaper used machine is bought while the line's varied capsule runs never fill its capacity
edge_cases.trigger: a low landed cost tempts a buy the utilisation cannot justify
edge_cases.mitigation: check the run profile against the breakeven; a varied capsule line below breakeven stays subcontracted

edge_cases.description: The HSN 8447 BCD/IGST or a 2025-26 budget change moves the duty stack after a plan is set
edge_cases.trigger: a duty or budget change touches knitting-machine imports
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm the exact BCD sub-heading at purchase and re-run the landed cost and breakeven through the review loop

workflow.description: Fix Phase 0 subcontract / Phase 1 buy-used-Chinese-first / new-later as the decision spine
workflow.gate: the phase order and the proven-volume trigger are stated

workflow.description: Justify subcontracting knit+link+finish into the mesh and owning only design, brand and a sampling hand-flat
workflow.gate: the agglomeration-is-infrastructure and capital-stays-free rationale is documented

workflow.action: Frame the India importer/dealer market and duty
workflow.description: Establish India as importer/dealer and the HSN 8447 duty stack on any imported machine
workflow.gate: India-as-importer and the HSN 8447 duty stack are documented

workflow.action: Consolidate the price bands per class
workflow.description: Lay down new/used bands per machine class as labeled estimates with confidence
workflow.gate: eight+ machine classes have new and used bands labeled estimate with confidence

workflow.action: Build the linker-bound throughput and capacity picture
workflow.description: Show linking caps output and that a buy must match linker and programmer capacity
workflow.gate: the per-shift bands show linking as the binding ceiling for a buy

workflow.action: Assemble the full landed cost stack
workflow.description: Add HSN 8447 duty plus freight, install, power/air and spares to the band price
workflow.gate: the full machine cost into the breakeven is defined beyond the sticker

workflow.description: Recompute breakeven_utilisation from labeled inputs and conclude where subcontract wins
workflow.gate: the breakeven formula is recomputed from labeled inputs with a below-breakeven conclusion

workflow.action: Set the buy-used and buy-new thresholds
workflow.description: State buy-used at proven volume (Chinese first) and buy-new only as a benchmark
workflow.gate: the proven-volume buy-used trigger and the rare-new threshold are stated

workflow.description: Apply condition, toolchain-lock, spares/service and landed-quote checks before commit
workflow.gate: all four diligence checks are listed as the gate before a committed buy

workflow.description: Label every figure [ESTIMATE]/[FACT]/[UNKNOWN] with method/basis/confidence and a quote path
workflow.gate: every money/throughput/breakeven figure is labeled and tidy anchors are downgraded to bands

workflow.description: Integrate subcontract / buy-used / new-rarely / build-never gated on the breakeven and a landed quote
workflow.gate: the composed verdict is gated on the breakeven and a landed quote with whole-garment as a later study

workflow.action: Set the acquisition review cadence and triggers
workflow.description: Define the review cadence and material-change triggers back to phases and the breakeven
workflow.gate: a cadence and explicit trigger list routing to ACQUISITION_PHASES and BREAKEVEN_UTILISATION exist

priority_rationale: The phased acquisition order, the Phase 0 subcontract posture and the India importer/duty frame come first because every buy decision depends on knowing the phase, the subcontract default and the import structure; the price bands, throughput/capacity, landed cost and breakeven build the economic core that gates owning iron; the buy-used/new thresholds, diligence and honesty discipline turn that core into a committable, honestly-costed decision; the composed verdict integrates them; and the review loop comes last because it watches the whole decision and routes material changes back to the phases and the breakeven.

dominance_rules.rule: The buy-vs-subcontract breakeven dominates any buy decision
dominance_rules.rationale: owning iron is only correct when utilisation clears the breakeven; below it subcontract is cheaper
dominance_rules.trigger: any plan to buy a machine
dominance_rules.action: recompute the breakeven on real rates and buy only if a repeating program clears it

dominance_rules.rationale: the core kinematic chain is decades-deep and supplier-defended; ~$2M-10M+/3-7yr buys a likely-inferior result
dominance_rules.action: rule out build and buy a sub-$20k working used machine instead

dominance_rules.rule: Securing the programmer and linkers dominates acquiring the machine
dominance_rules.rationale: a machine with no toolchain-matched programmer or matched linkers is dead iron
dominance_rules.trigger: a machine buy with no secured programmer or linker capacity
dominance_rules.action: secure or contract the programmer and linkers before committing the machine

dominance_rules.rule: Diligence and a landed quote dominate an attractive band price
dominance_rules.rationale: a band hides condition, toolchain-lock and import cost; a cheap band can become a stranded asset
dominance_rules.trigger: a used buy tempted by a low band price
dominance_rules.action: pass condition, toolchain, spares and a landed quote before committing

dominance_rules.rule: Honesty labeling dominates any cost figure
dominance_rules.rationale: a named-builder price stated as fact violates the binding honesty discipline and misleads planning
dominance_rules.trigger: any money or throughput figure entering the plan
dominance_rules.action: express it as a labeled [ESTIMATE]/[FACT]/[UNKNOWN] band with method/basis/confidence and a quote path

dominance_rules.rule: Used dominates new at the proven-volume buy
dominance_rules.rationale: the used pool is deep and post-Stoll deepening, the right capital intensity for a product/AI/export-edge brand
dominance_rules.trigger: a proven-volume buy considers new iron by default
dominance_rules.action: default to used Chinese Cixing-class; buy new only as a volume/quality benchmark

dominance_rules.rule: The linker-bound ceiling dominates knitting-machine count in sizing a buy
dominance_rules.rationale: linking not knitting caps daily output, so buying knitting capacity past the linker ceiling idles iron
dominance_rules.trigger: a buy sized off machine count
dominance_rules.action: size the buy off the linker-bound throughput and matched linker/programmer capacity

dominance_rules.rule: Confirming the exact 8447 duty dominates committing the landed cost
dominance_rules.rationale: the ~7.5% BCD sub-heading is a working estimate that moves the landed cost into the breakeven
dominance_rules.trigger: a landed cost is about to be committed on the working duty assumption
dominance_rules.action: confirm the exact BCD sub-heading at purchase before committing the landed cost

anti_rework_rules.rule: Recompute the buy-vs-subcontract breakeven before committing any buy
anti_rework_rules.prevents: owning iron at a utilisation where subcontract is cheaper

anti_rework_rules.rule: Secure a toolchain-matched programmer and matched linkers before buying a machine
anti_rework_rules.prevents: acquiring dead iron that cannot be programmed or its output linked

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pass condition, toolchain, spares and a landed quote before committing a used buy
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a cheap band price becoming a stranded asset after purchase

anti_rework_rules.rule: Add the HSN 8447 duty and hidden landed costs before using a machine cost
anti_rework_rules.prevents: under-budgeting an import by mistaking a band price for a landed price

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every cost/throughput figure estimate-or-fact-or-unknown when first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a labeled band being quoted downstream as a named-builder fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size every buy off the linker-bound ceiling, not knitting-machine count
anti_rework_rules.prevents: buying knitting capacity that outruns linkers and programmer and idles iron

anti_rework_rules.rule: Narrow any new-build to Shima or Chinese after the 2025 Stoll exit
anti_rework_rules.prevents: planning a new Stoll purchase that is no longer available

anti_rework_rules.rule: Open the whole-garment trade study only at sustained single-style volume
anti_rework_rules.prevents: buying the highest-capital steepest-programming class before volume justifies it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a style clears proven repeating volume
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the breakeven and the buy-used decision and size the buy off linker capacity

iteration_protocol.trigger: a real landed used-machine quote arrives (the #1 input gap into T4)
iteration_protocol.action: replace the estimate band, re-run the landed cost and the breakeven

iteration_protocol.trigger: job-work knit/link per-piece rates become available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the conversion-saving input and re-run the breakeven and verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: the HSN 8447 BCD/IGST or a 2025-26 budget change moves the duty
iteration_protocol.action: confirm the exact sub-heading and re-run the landed cost and breakeven

iteration_protocol.trigger: the Stoll-exit used-pool effect or ex-Stoll service cost settles
iteration_protocol.action: update the used-pool depth and ex-Stoll diligence and re-run the buy decision

iteration_protocol.trigger: programmer or linker availability or cost shifts
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the binding capacity and the breakeven period_capacity input

iteration_protocol.trigger: a single style's volume justifies a whole-garment trade study
iteration_protocol.action: open the whole-garment trade study against the panelled used-plus-linkers baseline
